answer: We formalize a Sybil-resistant mechanism where validators must commit a dynamic staking collateral B to a trellis of state transitions, meaning any attempt to forge concurrent identities on the consensus river triggers a subgame-perfect slashing penalty S > B. If an adversary deploys k identities, the zero-knowledge verifiable delay function imposes a cumulative opportunity cost that outpaces the expected reward function R(k), forcing the net utility to be strictly negative. Thus, honest replication remains the unique Nash equilibrium.
